correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md lines 23–70. Character orthogonality gives q^(-3) times the sum of squared triple-fiber sums. With w=a+b and v=a−b, the second constraint becomes u=s²+sw−v², so the fiber cardinalities are q at s≠0 and q, 2q or 0 as stated at s=0. The squared cardinalities sum to q⁴+q³−q². Unit modulus gives the upper bound, with equality exactly when triple phases align separately in each fiber. The diagonal (0,0) fiber forces cube roots after removing the common phase. Translating zero-sum triples makes each first phase difference additive after subtracting its value at zero, yielding a symmetric F_3-bilinear polarization B. Comparing (t,1−t,0) with (v,v,1+v), v=t²−t, gives B(t,t)=B(1,t²); polarizing gives B(a,b)=B(1,ab). Nondegeneracy of the field trace yields precisely linear-plus-quadratic field trace phases, and also makes the q² normalized classes distinct. Every such phase attains equality. This covers fixed nontrivial additive character and the claimed d≥2, not unrestricted L² extremizers.
